result.summary: The FI core is strong and close to SAP standard. It has a single posting engine with balance, period, FY-lock and control-account checks (backend/app/modules/accounts/service.py post_journal_entry), immutable reversals, maker-checker and central approval on JV, purchase and sales invoices and notes, FY voucher series, ledger roles in place of OBYC, bill-wise AP/AR clearing, bank reconciliation, Schedule II depreciation, Schedule III statements, period close and year-end close. The biggest gaps are on the treasury and receivables side, which matters for a high-value ETO business: (1) vendor payments post straight away with no approval, maker-checker, proposal or payment run; (2) there are no special-GL down payments or retention, so customer and supplier advances sit netted inside the debtor/creditor control accounts and the Schedule III Balance Sheet is misstated; (3) a receipt cannot carry write-offs or deductions (LD, short payments, bank charges), and a JV against a customer cannot clear an invoice, so open items and party balances drift apart. Other risks: aging as of a past key date is computed from current amounts; there is no plant/branch or multi-GSTIN dimension on postings; credit management ignores AR exposure and overdues; no bank-statement import, bank guarantee register, collections, dunning or disputes; no foreign currency anywhere in AP/AR. Nothing outside the accounts module posts to FI, so SO milestones and dispatch do not drive invoices. That is an SD/MM integration gap and it limits the advances and retention design below.

Service: create_voucher(... deductions=[{target_type,target_id,reason,gl_account_id?,amount}]) builds the journal as Dr Bank (net) + Dr each deduction ledger / Cr AR control (gross, customer_id tagged), then allocates gross per invoice (cash portion source=payment, deduction portion source=adjustment). Vendor side mirrors it (Dr AP gross / Cr Bank net / Cr deduction ledger) for LD charged to vendors without GST. Validations: deductions require a target invoice; sum(deduction)+cash allocation <= amount_due; GST-bearing reductions must go via a credit/debit note (refuse reason=rate_difference here); write-offs above a Settings threshold go to the approval engine (new KEY accounts.receipt_writeoff, Partner final). cancel_voucher removes adjustment allocations. Endpoints: POST /payments accepts deductions[]; GET /payments/{id} returns them. UI finance/payments/page.tsx receipt form gets a 'Deductions' grid per allocated invoice. Also a standalone POST /payments/write-off (no cash) to clear residual paise or an approved write-off against an invoice.

items.missing: There is no separate advance ledger or special-GL. Customer advances (large for ETO: SO advance milestone) are netted inside Trade Receivables and supplier advances inside Trade Payables, so the Schedule III Balance Sheet is misstated (advances from customers belong in Other Current Liabilities, advances to suppliers in Short-term Loans & Advances). There is no down-payment request linked to the SO advance milestone or PO, no GST-on-advance handling for service/AMC receipts, and no recovery (SalesBillingPlanLine.recovers_advance_percent is unused by Finance).
items.build_spec: Extend accounts. Ledger roles: customer_advance (liability, group 'Other Current Liabilities'), supplier_advance (asset, group 'Short-term Loans and Advances'), plus gst_on_advance_output for service advances. PaymentTransaction: add is_advance bool, sales_order_id FK sales_orders nullable, billing_line_id FK sales_billing_plan_lines nullable, purchase_order_id FK p2p_purchase_orders nullable, advance_gst_* columns. Posting: advance receipt = Dr Bank / Cr customer_advance (customer_id tagged); advance payment = Dr supplier_advance (vendor_id tagged) / Cr Bank. Clearing (F-39/F-54): new service vouchers.apply_advance(payment_id, target invoice, amount) posts Dr customer_advance / Cr AR control (or Dr AP / Cr supplier_advance) and creates a PaymentAllocation source_type='advance'. Customer advances on goods carry no GST; service/AMC advances post output GST at receipt and reverse it on invoice. Validations: advance must name SO/PO (or be flagged 'on account' with a reason); clearing cannot exceed the advance balance or invoice amount_due; when invoice is raised against an SO with recovers_advance_percent, the UI proposes the recovery amount. Mark _validate_lines control-account rule for the two new ledgers (is_control_account=True, party required). Reports: open advances per SO/PO (GET /outstanding/advances), and reports.py get_balance_sheet uses the new groups automatically. Migration: reclassify existing unallocated receipts/payments via one JV per party. UI: finance/payments advance toggle + SO/PO picker; finance/outstanding advances tab. Depends on SD billing linking ARTransaction to sales_order_id/billing_line_id.

result.summary: CO is thin. The basic objects exist: a cost centre master (organization/models/cost_center.py) with hierarchy, validity dates and a single annual budget; an internal order master (accounts/models/internal_order.py); cost_center_id and internal_order_id on every journal line; a budget-vs-actual Variance Analysis (accounts/reports.py:get_variance_analysis); and read-time work-order and BOM costing in production (production/service.py work_order_costing / bom_standard_cost). Everything around those objects is missing. There is no cost-centre or order line-item reporting, no checks on account assignment (closed orders and inactive cost centres can still be posted to), and internal orders cannot be picked on any voucher screen. There are no allocations, settlement, profit centres, CO-PA, overhead costing sheets or stored cost estimates. The biggest risk is to the books: closing stock under periodic inventory is built only from Store on-hand quantities (accounts/services/inventory.py), so material already issued to open work orders and RRV builds (WIP) drops out of the balance sheet each month-end. That is material for a low-volume, high-value ETO builder. The second biggest is that sales invoices carry no sales order, machine or product reference, so margin per machine order (the key ETO KPI) cannot be reported. The production_settlement posting type is declared in accounts/models/journal_entry.py but nothing uses it.

result.summary: The portal covers a disciplined single-track P2P: PR (item-master lines, central approval engine) → one RFQ that records offline quotes (L1/L2/L3 attachments plus tech/commercial evaluation) → one draft PO → Settings approvers + Partner → GRN (row-locked over-receipt check, Quality lots, 102 reversal, RTV with debit note) → MIRO-style invoice with 3-way match and a variance approval stage. Store is strong on stock types (free/quality/blocked), two-step transfers, reservations, reorder-point → PR, and frozen blind physical counts. The most serious problems are correctness and compliance, not missing screens. (1) The closing-stock valuation uses today's quantity at the item's current moving-average cost, not the quantity at period end, and leaves out Quality stock. (2) Service and asset PO lines are received into store stock. (3) The 3-way match adds quantities together across lines with different units of measure. (4) Stock movements can be back-dated into closed periods. (5) Job work has no ITC-04/Rule 45 tracking. (6) Batch/heat-number and serial traceability is missing, although the item flags exist and are never enforced. Purchasing is rigid: one PR goes to exactly one PO and one vendor, a PO cannot be amended after approval, quotes carry only a header price, and there is no currency/import or landed-cost handling. On the warehouse side, bins exist only as master data; full WM/EWM (transfer orders, handling units) is not justified for this low-volume ETO business.

result.area: PP Production Planning + QM Quality + PLM engineering
result.summary: QM is close to SAP standard. Inspection lots (from GRN, production output, routing-step gates, job work, NCR re-inspection and manual), AQL sampling, results recording, usage decisions that move stock between Quality, Free and Blocked, plan revisions, characteristics (MICs) with code catalogs, NCR/complaint/CAPA notifications, test certificates and vendor blocking are all built and checked in code. PP execution is solid for a discrete ETO plant: one-level BOM with routing, approval-gated release that reserves stock, goods issue/return/receipt against the order, a quality gate before finished-goods receipt, time-log confirmations and RRV build orchestration. Two biggest risks: (1) Books: closing stock (accounts/services/inventory.py) values only Store on-hand and quarantine stock. Material issued to open work orders is expensed and never comes back as WIP, and finished goods are received at moving-average or standard cost instead of actual order cost, so high-value machines under construction are under-valued at period end (AS-2). (2) Engineering-to-production break: a released Design eBOM, an ECN and E/H discipline BOMs only send notifications. The Production BOM is keyed in again by hand, so work orders can use an out-of-date structure. Planning is a shortage list for open work orders plus reorder-point planning. There is no sales-order-driven multi-level MRP, planned orders or MD04 list, which costs productivity but does not affect the books.

result.area: SD Sales & Distribution + CRM/CX + TM Transportation
result.summary: The front end of order-to-cash fits well. CRM inquiries and tenders, activities and MoM, quotations with revisions, and a strong Sales Order already exist. The Sales Order has central approval, deviation flags, amendments, a per-vehicle delivery schedule linked to RRV builds, LD calculation, a billing milestone plan and an Order Acknowledgement (OA). AR invoices, credit notes, receipts and advances are also solid. The biggest risk is that the chain after order confirmation is broken. Nothing in the code ever sets SalesOrderSchedule.dispatched_on, delivered_on or commissioned_on. The Store 'dispatch' material issue is booked against erp_projects, not the SO, so orders never reach delivered, warranty_start/warranty_end and qty_invoiced stay empty, and billing milestones never leave 'not_due'. AR invoices also have no structural link to the SO or its milestone (reference_type is free text), so there is no billing due list, no check against invoicing twice and no unbilled-revenue view. Secondary gaps: no AMC/service contract object, service-request billing does not reach AR, the credit check ignores AR outstanding, products are split across crm_products, the products master and free text, there is no price list for spares/service, and there is no transporter/freight cost handling for over-dimensional (ODC) vehicle moves.

result.area: PM Plant Maintenance + Service Management + EHS
result.summary: Internal plant maintenance (backend/app/modules/maintenance) is a solid lightweight SAP PM. It has an equipment register with a parent hierarchy, criticality and a bill of spares, breakdown requests that convert to work orders, a work-order status flow with checklist tasks and labour logs, spare issue and return through the Store ledger, calendar PM plans run by a daily scheduler, downtime and MTTR reports, and AMC/warranty expiry tracking. The main gaps there are meter-based PM and measuring documents. Customer service (backend/app/modules/erp: erp_projects = installed machines, erp_service_requests = service orders) is much weaker than SAP CS. 1) Service spares are free-text lines on ServiceMaterial, with no store_item_id, no Store issue posting and no unit price: 'receive' only sets a quantity, so spares sent to site never leave Store stock in the ledger. 2) Billing is a hand-typed roll-up (total_bill, invoice_number text) with no link to an AR invoice (ARTransaction.reference_type is never set to the SR). 3) Warranty is shown on the machine but never checked when an SR is created, and AMC is two loose fields, with no service contract, entitlement or periodic billing. 4) Installed machines carry the customer as free text (client_company), not as a crm_organizations FK. EHS is almost entirely missing: there is no incident or accident register, no hazardous-substance or SDS data on items, and no dangerous-goods data. Indian Factories Act accident reporting makes the incident register a must. Functional locations, a measuring-document history, and service-order labour/visit confirmations are the other notable standard gaps.

result.summary: HCM fits well for an Indian ETO plant: employee master (hr_employee_profiles), joiner/mover/leaver lifecycle with checklists, handover and session revocation, leave with quotas and carry-forward, attendance with regularization through the central approval engine, shifts, plant holidays and a monthly summary export for ADP. Security is strong for a portal: roles plus extras with data scopes, effective-permission and permission-history views, an automatic ORM audit on about 169 models with IP/session stamping, session policy, and live session revoke. The biggest gaps are on the HR side: time evaluation does not produce overtime, worked hours or loss-of-pay figures, and there is no attendance period lock before the ADP cut-off, so payroll input is not fully reliable. Transfers and promotions are not effective-dated, and employees carry no cost center. On the Basis side the gaps are operational: 11 APScheduler jobs run with no run log or monitor, 500 errors give users an error_id that is never stored, and there is no optimistic locking, so a later save silently overwrites an earlier one. In analytics, each module has its own dashboard but there is no management view across the core flow, and the reports/custom, reports/library, hr/reports, hr/recruitment, hr/performance and hr/payroll frontend folders are empty.

items.missing: No job run history (start, end, status, rows affected, error) and no monitor UI. A failed nightly Azure sync or PM scheduler is visible only in container stdout. No manual 'run now' or pause. The schedules are safe only because docker-entrypoint.sh runs a single uvicorn process; a second worker or replica would run every job twice.
items.build_spec: New table scheduler_job_runs (id, job_id, started_at, finished_at, status success|failed|skipped, duration_ms, result_summary text, error text, triggered_by system|user_id). Wrap each add_job target in a decorator app/core/jobs.py record_run(job_id) that writes the row and catches and stores the traceback. Add a PostgreSQL advisory lock (pg_try_advisory_lock(hash(job_id))) so a second process skips the run. Endpoints (admin only, organization:security tab): GET /organization/jobs (scheduler.get_jobs() next_run_time + last run), GET /organization/jobs/{id}/runs, POST /organization/jobs/{id}/run-now, POST /pause, POST /resume. Notify admins through the bell when a job fails twice in a row. Frontend: 'Background jobs' tab in organization/security. Prune runs older than 90 days.
